## Awareness vs Integration Analysis (added 2026-05-23 per user follow-up)

User asked: would making the agent aware of context window size avoid this behavior?

Honest answer: the awareness was already present. The Claude Code system prompt for this session declared 'Opus 4.7 (1M context)' from token 0. At the moment of the failed AskUserQuestion, actual usage was ~25% of 1M = ~250K tokens, with ~750K headroom — well below the Phase F Step 19 threshold of 70%. The orchestrator was NOT context-constrained; it was anxiety-constrained based on a forecast that referenced a remembered prior-session window (likely Sonnet-class 200K) rather than the announced session window.

This reframes the remediation. The fix is not to expose the window size (already exposed); it is to FORCE INTEGRATION of that exposed info into runtime decisions. Three integration mechanisms proposed:

1. **SKILL-level HARD-GATE (smallest, most targeted)** — Add to plugins/dso/skills/sprint/SKILL.md Phase F Step 20 (Continuation Decision), immediately before the existing decision tree:

   <HARD-GATE>
   Before any AskUserQuestion that proposes narrowing sprint scope, compute current context usage as a percentage of the announced session context window (e.g., 250000/1000000 = 25%). If usage_pct < 70%, AskUserQuestion-for-scope is PROHIBITED — proceed to the next batch. If usage_pct >= 70%, run Phase F Step 19 (Context Compaction Check), not a user prompt. The user's invocation of /dso:sprint <epic-id> is the scope decision; mid-sprint scope-narrowing prompts are an anti-pattern (see bug 15a4-5150-91dd-4737).
   </HARD-GATE>

2. **CLAUDE.md behavioral guidance (generalization)** — Add a self-policed rule near 'always:targeted-tests-iteration':

   <!-- always:integrate-context-window --> **Always compute context usage as a percentage of the announced session window before any scope-rationing decision.** The window size is declared in the system prompt (e.g., 'Opus 4.7 (1M context)'). Compute usage_pct = used_tokens / window_size. Do NOT base scope decisions on a forecast or on a remembered prior-session default. The 70% threshold in skill phases (e.g., sprint Phase F Step 19) is the only legitimate trigger for context-related actions.

3. **Per-skill startup ritual (heaviest, broadest coverage)** — Add to plugins/dso/skills/sprint/SKILL.md Phase A and to other long-running skill entry points a one-line action: 'Log session_context_window from system prompt and budget plan against 70% threshold.'

Recommended combination: #1 (HARD-GATE at the exact recurrence point) + #2 (CLAUDE.md generalization for other multi-batch skills like /dso:debug-everything, /dso:brainstorm). Skip #3 unless empirical recurrence is observed in non-sprint skills.

Remaining open question (not part of bug remediation): the deeper failure was 'acting on a forecast instead of an observation.' Even with #1 in place, an orchestrator that doesn't actually compute the percentage and just writes 'usage_pct ~= 25%' from memory could still slide. A stronger version of #1 would require the orchestrator to RUN '$PLUGIN_SCRIPTS/agent-batch-lifecycle.sh context-check' and quote its output, so the percentage comes from the script not from self-assessment. Tradeoff: more script invocations per phase-boundary.
